🛍️The Furugi Festival at Tokyo Big Sight in Odaiba is Japan’s largest vintage clothing extravaganza, held annually at the iconic convention center. 

Spanning vast exhibition halls, it features over 200 stalls from renowned vintage shops like Jam and Berberjin to individual sellers, offering retro kimonos, 80s streetwear, and rare accessories. 🛒

The event draws throngs of stylish youth—fashion students, influencers, and eco-conscious shoppers—eager to score unique, sustainable finds. 

With a lively atmosphere and a 500-yen entry fee, it’s a must-visit for anyone passionate about vintage fashion.🤑".
transcription: Oh god, look at it. It's perfect.

Japan, day 5 🇯🇵 

I knew Osaka was known as Japan’s Kitchen, but I didn’t realise it was going to be this good.

transcription: If you love food, I have no doubt that you will love Osaka in Japan. It is known as Japan's kitchen, but I just didn't really realize how good it would actually be. Whenever I go away, the trip normally does revolve around food and finding all the really cool places. That's exactly what we did. I started out wanting an outlaw coffee. This was so cute and they have a mucher espresso drink that's gone viral. But I also recommend trying the cinnamon scrolls. In five days and we haven't yet done any shopping, so we made sure to do that. If you're coming to Japan and you're wanting to get shoes of some sort, have them in mind before you get here because I can tell you right now it is so overwhelming. is then a restaurant in Osaka called Yucaniku Katana is quite popular because they do these wagyu beef bowls for lunch but only 20 Australian dollars and they are amazing. A little tip for you don't go to the dot-on-buri location so we went there first there was a line they ended up selling out but when we went to the other location there was no cute at all and we got a table straight away. I popped the address on the screen just in case the same thing happens to you. We spent the afternoon shopping and then thought we deserved nothing but a gourmet meal from McDonald's. Right McDonald's in Japan has to have been on my bucket list for so many years after seeing it on social media because it just looked so good. Shrimp burger and the shrapnel shake shake chicken had to be my two favorites.
